# 4k-minecraft

> A remake of Notch's 2009 Minecraft 4K as one self-extracting HTML page of at most 4096 bytes, rendered with WebGPU. A 1024x1024x128 voxel world is generated and ray-marched per pixel by a single compute shader. Made by Pierre Roy (Ayfri).

Not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft. Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Synergies AB.

## Play

- [Play the game](https://4k-minecraft.ayfri.com/): the 4 KB page itself, click to lock the pointer and play.
- [About page](https://4k-minecraft.ayfri.com/about): screenshot, features, controls and browser requirements in plain HTML.
- [Source code](https://github.com/Ayfri/4k-minecraft): the game, the shader and the build that packs them, under the GPL 3.0.
- [4k-minecraft: A Deflate Stream Without 10 Bytes](https://ayfri.com/articles/minecraft-in-four-kilobytes/index.md): the article on how the page packs the game, the 10 forbidden bytes and the deflate search that avoids them.

## What it is

Notch's entry for the Java 4K contest (December 2009) was 2581 bytes: a 64x64x63 world drawn by a CPU raycaster. This version keeps the idea and moves world generation and rendering to the GPU: a 1024x1024x128 world (one byte per cell) is generated by a compute shader at load, and the same shader marches a ray through the voxels for every pixel and writes it into the canvas texture.

## The 4096-byte constraint

The whole game, shaders included, fits in one HTML file: 4085 of 4096 bytes. How the packing works:

- The page is `<meta charset=l9>`, a `<body onload>` decoder and a `<canvas id=c>` holding an `<xmp>` element, whose raw text is the compressed stream.
- The decoder reads the stream back as bytes, pipes it through `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` and passes the inflated script to `eval`.
- An in-house deflate encoder searches the exact bit stream for one without the 10 bytes the HTML parser or `l9` would change, so the decoder needs no unescaping. Escaped zopfli and libdeflate streams compete with it: every candidate is packed into a full page and the smallest page wins.
- The JavaScript and the WGSL shader are minified by an in-house build, and the shader shares its numeric constants with the game code.

## Features

- World of 1024x1024x128 cells wrapping around on x and z: lakes, beaches, deserts, plains, forests, a snow-capped mountain massif, caves, trees, flowers, grass tufts and coal, iron and diamond ores.
- Physics: gravity, jumping, wall and ceiling collisions, swimming, one-block climbing.
- Rendering: voxel ray marching at the full window resolution, procedural 16x16 textures, ambient occlusion, sun shadows, see-through leaves, glass, a day and night cycle with stars, fog, underwater tint, a targeted-block outline and a crosshair.
- Blocks: break the targeted block (reach of 6 blocks) and place the selected one in front of it.

## Controls

- Click: lock the pointer. Mouse: look around.
- W A S D: walk (physical keys, so Z Q S D on AZERTY).
- Left Shift: sprint at 1.3x speed.
- Space: jump, swim up in water.
- Left click: break the targeted block. Right click: place the selected block.
- 1 to 9 and 0: select grass, dirt, stone, sand, log, leaves, planks, bricks, snow or glass.
- Mouse wheel: cycle the selected block through everything placeable: the red flower, the yellow flower, the tuft, the ten blocks above, then coal, iron and diamond.
- A 48 px preview of the selected block sits in the bottom-right corner.

## Browser requirements

WebGPU with immediates (`setImmediates` and `var<immediate>`), a keyboard and a mouse.

- Chrome 150+ on Windows: runs (tested on Chrome 155, no flag).
- Chrome 150+ on macOS: runs (tested by a player).
- Edge 150+, Chrome 150+ on Linux and ChromeOS: untested, same engine.
- Firefox 158: does not run, no immediates (tested on Windows, every other feature works).
- Safari 26: does not run, no immediates.
- Phones and tablets: no keyboard and mouse controls.
